t: This is the Memorial to the Great Exhibition, just south of the Royal Albert Hall. It commemorates the Great Exhibition of 1851 and shows Prince Albert, the Prince Consort. The sculptor Joseph Durham designed it, with modifications by the architect Sydney Smirke. It was first put up in 1863 in the Royal Horticultural Society gardens. When those gardens were rebuilt and Prince Consort Road was created, it was moved to where it stands now, between 1891 and 1893.
